text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 2.3.0 runtime roll we’re seeing a consistent +11% p95 latency on the conversational workload using AWQ weight-only int8. Appears in US-west only, reproduces on canary cluster.
perf-bot: AUTO: perf/regression detected for build=2.3.0, test=conv-1k, metric=p95_latency, delta=+11% (baseline=82ms -> 91ms). See /artifacts/2951112222/trace.html
devon: Any quick Profiler captures? suspecting pack/unpack hotpath or KV cache prefetch thrash.
maria: I ran a microprofile on canary. Short excerpt:
```
kernel,phase,call_count,avg_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms
awq_pack,pack,1024,0.42,0.40,0.92
awq_unpack,unpack,1024,0.18,0.15,0.35
kv_prefetch,walk,512,1.20,1.10,2.40
attention_kv,lookup,2048,0.05,0.04,0.12
scheduler,staggered_batch,256,0.60,0.58,1.05
```
Note the `kv_prefetch` spikes on some requests; correlates with p95 tails.
ton y: Hmm the `staggered_batch` worker time looks high. Did group_size change in the calibration for AWQ?
maria: We bumped group_size from 16->32 during AWQ recalib (to reduce quant error). That reduces compute but increases pack buffer churn and makes the pack path longer for small sequences.
alexa: Also observed that our packing hysteresis (we only repack after buffer hits 768 bytes) makes tiny chat messages wait longer — that increases latency variance. Staggered batching + hysteresis interaction could be the root.
kevin: Quick mitigation idea: lower pack hysteresis and enable 'kv_stride_prefetch=adaptive' which narrows prefetch window on high-LRU churn. Sample config: 
```
runtime:
  awq:
    group_size: 24
    pack_hysteresis_bytes: 512
    kv_stride_prefetch: adaptive
    sampler: staggered_v2
```
devon: Can you run an A/B with group_size=24 and hysteresis 512 on canary? Also capture KV cache hit/miss by key-range.
maria: Started a canary now (job id: canary-2951112222b). Early numbers: baseline p95=91ms, canary p95=84ms (-7.7%). CPU spikiness reduced. Memory overhead up ~3% due to slightly more frequent repack.
ton y: Good improvement. Any difference in cold-cache flows? I worry about cold short chats hitting fp8 fallback path vs int8.
maria: Cold-cache still worse by ~5% vs baseline. Looks like prefetch warmup is the main factor — cold requests trigger wider KV prefetch which activates a slower memcpy path.
alexa: For long term: consider kernel chooser policy update: prefer `awq_pack_serial` for group_size<=24 and `awq_pack_parallel` otherwise. Add a fast-path for cold-cache: small-seq fast-unpack that avoids full kv_prefetch for first token.
kevin: I can prototype the kernel chooser rule in runtime/packing/chooser.cc — should be a few lines: check group_size and cache_state bitfield.
perf-bot: NOTE: will run perf regression gate on next PR if change touches runtime/packing.
devon: Prefer to land config change first (non-code) to buy time. Then iterate kernel chooser.
maria: Plan posted in ticket: https://redwood/issue/INF-8812 — 1) deploy group_size=24 + hysteresis=512 to prod-canary, 2) monitor p50/p95 + kv_miss ratio, 3) implement kernel chooser v1 as code change, 4) add unit microbench for cold-cache memcpy path.
ton y: +1. If canary holds for 24h we can roll to 25% traffic.
alexa: Also flagging eval team: recalibration quality checks vs AWQ group_size changes (we decreased group_size slightly, need to run eval set to ensure no regressions). @ml-evals
maria: thanks all — will update thread with canary metrics. :thumbsup:
